If you cut Shorts from podcasts or interviews, most of the clock time is not creative. It is the same checklist: find a 30-second stretch that stands on its own, drop the dead air, reframe to 9:16, put the face in the middle, burn in captions, add a hook title, maybe a zoom and a sound on the punch word. That checklist is regular enough to automate on your own machine.

I will be honest about what this replaces and what it does not.
A useful default is six clips, each 20–60 seconds (30–45 is the sweet spot), already i…
articles.title: Build a local Python pipeline that turns a long talk into six 9:16 Shorts

articles.author: DiziGoo Digital
articles.description:
More people now ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity instead of typing into Google. If your site blocks those crawlers or explains itself badly, you will not be mentioned. At DiziGoo, a digital marketing and software company in Bareilly, India, we made our own site AI-friendly and these are the steps that mattered.
Check your robots.txt. If you want to be cited in AI answers, allow the bots that fetch pages for answers, such as GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended. Also check your CDN: some platforms add their own managed robots.txt that can override yours, so open /robots.txt in a browser after every change.
llms.txt is a plain text file at the root of your site that summarises who you are, what you offer and your best pages, written for machines. Keep it factual: business name, location, services, links to guides, contact details.
Use schema.org JSON-LD for Organization, LocalBusiness, Service, FAQPage and BreadcrumbList. Keep the name, address and phone identical to your Google Business Profile. Machines trust data that matches everywhere.
AI answers quote pages that answer one question clearly. Use short headings that are real questions, answer in the first two sentences, and keep facts like services, locations and timelines in text, not only in images.
Claim your Google Business Profile, Bing Places and company directories, and publish helpful articles. OpenAI has also started Businesses in ChatGPT, where a company can claim a verified profile. We have started that process too.
Search your brand and your service plus your city in an AI assistant once a week, and note whether you are mentioned. Fix the page that should have answered.
None of this needs a big budget, only consistency. More on how we approach AI search and SEO: https://dizigoo.com/services/seo/
By Akash Gupta, founder of DiziGoo (digital marketing, websites, software and AI automation), Bareilly and Pilibhit, India.
articles.title: Make your website readable by AI search: robots.txt, llms.txt and schema

Short answer: use multipart upload for large Node.js backup archives, and keep the upload ledger in your job database so a worker can resume, complete, or deliberately abort the transfer.
The deciding constraint is throughput under interruption. A developer-tools platform may turn thousands of receipt images and records into one tar.gz, then retain that exact file for an audit. Holding the archive in memory or restarting one giant PUT after a broken connection makes the retry unit needlessly large. Multipart changes the retry unit from “the whole audit archive” to “one numbered part.”
This is an operational choice, not a promise that multipart wins for every object. Small receipts can stay on a single PUT. Large backup bundles should not.
Picture the original worker as a three-box diagram …

articles.author: LukasSchmidt295
articles.description:
For an edtech shipment-update fan-out, use at-least-once delivery with idempotent subscriber sends, a small retry budget, exponential backoff with jitter, and a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for exhausted jobs. That is the least complex policy that keeps a temporary downstream failure from becoming either a lost notification or an infinite retry loop.
The important choice is the unit of work. Create one immutable job per subscriber, not one job for the whole shipment audience. A worker can then acknowledge successful subscribers independently while delaying only the failed ones. The shipment event carries a stable ID; each child job adds the subscriber ID and channel. A unique delivery key ties those values together, so a redelivery can be recognized without pretending the queue provides exactly…
